why_ai: Specimens are tested on physical analysers under a CLIA director's accountability and pathologists sign diagnoses, while ageing and genetic testing keep demand growing; most routine testing is a commodity bought on network and price.
why_clarity: Each test follows a written procedure, produces an exact number checked by quality control and proficiency testing, and repeats thousands of times a day.
why_digital: The work starts from a tube or tissue delivered by courier and ends as a digital result; practices choose labs on insurance networks, couriers and interfaces, mostly locally.

why_ai: Claim building, scrubbing and denial work are document and rules tasks that billing software and agents absorb; only coverage strategy needs senior judgement.
why_clarity: Claims are paid or denied against written rules, at enormous volume, with outcomes known within weeks.
why_digital: Requisition data, claims and remittances are electronic and the work is done remotely, often outsourced.

why_ai: Computing expected payment from a public fee schedule and contract terms is arithmetic that software does better than people.
why_clarity: Every line has an exact expected amount under the contract, so variance is objective and checked on each remittance.
why_digital: Fee schedule files, contracts and 835 remittances are all digital, and recovery work is done remotely.

why_ai: Policy matching and submissions automate, but building coverage evidence and winning appeals on high-dollar tests still needs experienced reimbursement staff.
why_clarity: Payer criteria are written down, yet they differ by payer and change often, and appeal outcomes take months.
why_digital: Portals, policies, records and appeals move electronically between lab, practice and payer.

why_ai: Outreach runs couriers, draw sites and a hospital lab for local practices, where service relationships and network status keep clients loyal.
why_clarity: Turnaround, interface uptime and retained clients are measurable, and the same routine tests recur daily.
why_digital: Specimens travel physically from local practices, while orders and results flow through EHR interfaces; clients are local.

why_ai: Drivers physically collect specimens from offices and lockboxes on local roads, which autonomy will not replace for most routes by 2031.
why_clarity: Routes, pickup times and rejection rates are countable every day against fixed stability limits.
why_digital: The work is moving physical specimens between local sites by vehicle.

why_ai: A licensed pathologist must make and sign each diagnosis and carries the liability, and the specialty is short-staffed.
why_clarity: Reports follow synoptic formats on recurring specimen types, but pathologists differ at the margins and errors surface late through amendments and outcomes.
why_digital: Tissue and glass are physical, but digitised slides can be read remotely and reports are delivered digitally.

why_ai: Small labs test specimens on site under a CLIA director's legal responsibility, close to the practice's patients.
why_clarity: CLIA and accreditor requirements are a written checklist, and quality control passes or fails daily.
why_digital: Testing is hands-on in the office; records and results are increasingly digital but the lab serves its own practice.

why_ai: Phlebotomists draw frail patients at the bedside in homes and nursing homes, where skill and familiarity with residents matter.
why_clarity: A draw is completed on time or not, though vein access and refusals make each patient different.
why_digital: The service is delivered by hand at the patient's bedside on local routes.

why_ai: Releasing results is accountable work for licensed staff, but rules and learned models are taking over most of the decisions.
why_clarity: Rules are written down and results are reviewed by the thousand, yet the judgement on held results is tacit and its truth often never confirmed.
why_digital: Results, rules and review queues are entirely digital inside middleware and the LIS.

why_ai: Someone must handle the tubes, but reading requisitions and matching orders is mechanical work that document AI absorbs.
why_clarity: Each specimen is either registered completely and correctly or not, thousands of times a day.
why_digital: Tubes and paper requisitions are physical; orders and LIS records are digital.

why_ai: Cohorts and studies are digital analysis, but the unique results corpus and pharma's need for regulatory-grade evidence sustain demand.
why_clarity: Datasets and studies have defined specifications, but methods vary by question and the value is judged slowly by clients.
why_digital: De-identified data in, datasets and studies out, sold remotely to drug developers.

why_ai: CLIA mandates participation in approved programmes, and providers must manufacture and ship physical challenge specimens.
why_clarity: Each lab's result is graded against peers on identical samples, a precise and repeated procedure.
why_digital: Specimens are made and shipped physically, while results and reports are digital and sold nationally.

why_ai: Payer policy tracking and denial analytics are digital work that software and language models increasingly do.
why_clarity: Denials, appeals and payments are recorded per claim, so analysis is checkable against outcomes within weeks.
why_digital: Claims and remittance data in, analytics and alerts out, delivered remotely.

why_ai: Testing-rate analytics for pharma are data work on contributed data, though brand teams value interpreters who know the lab landscape.
why_clarity: Analyses answer defined commercial questions, but methods vary and the effect on drug uptake is judged slowly.
why_digital: Data in and analysis out, sold remotely to pharma worldwide.

why_ai: Curating evidence on variants needs expert reading and judgement, though language models now accelerate literature curation.
why_clarity: Curation follows ACMG criteria and a recurring evidence format, but the truth about a variant's pathogenicity settles over years.
why_digital: Literature in, curated databases out, licensed online.

why_ai: Trial specimens must be tested physically under validated methods, and sponsors stay with labs they trust for multi-year studies.
why_clarity: Methods, kits and data transfers are specified in protocols and repeated across thousands of samples.
why_digital: Specimens ship in physically from trial sites worldwide; datasets go out digitally to sponsors who buy globally.

why_ai: Cataloguing tests and reading policies are document tasks that language models increasingly perform.
why_clarity: Catalogue entries and policy mappings are checkable against sources and updated in a repeated way.
why_digital: Public listings and policies in, structured data out, sold online.

why_ai: Policy writing and claim edits automate, but coverage decisions carry accountability that keeps clinicians in the loop.
why_clarity: Policies and edits are written rules applied to high claim volumes, with appeals and overturns as feedback.
why_digital: Claims, requests and policies are processed electronically for remote health plan clients.

why_ai: Inspectors visit labs in person and accreditation carries deemed regulatory authority that labs cannot do without.
why_clarity: Checklists define requirements, but findings depend on inspectors and their effect on lab quality is slow to show.
why_digital: Inspections are on site, while checklists, reports and decisions are digital and national.

why_ai: Hospital executives buy the advisers' judgement and transaction experience on one-off decisions.
why_clarity: Each valuation or strategy is bespoke and its correctness is known only years after the deal.
why_digital: Client data in, models and reports out, with on-site meetings for the decision.

why_ai: Several states license laboratory personnel and employers require board certification, and demand for bench scientists is not shrinking the way coding work is, so the credential keeps its value; the body itself is not the relationship buyers pay for.
why_clarity: Exams follow defined competency frameworks and are scored psychometrically, but certification is a proxy for competence whose accuracy shows only on the job.
why_digital: Exams are computer-based at test centres and credentials are managed online nationally.

why_ai: FDA and CLIA validation require accountable scientific evidence, but model building is the work AI tools accelerate most.
why_clarity: Models are evaluated on held-out slides with clear metrics, repeated per organ system.
why_digital: Digitised slides in, software out, sold remotely.

why_ai: Coverage decisions are accountable government determinations on novel evidence that carry real consequences for labs and patients.
why_clarity: Assessment criteria are published, but each test's evidence is different and the right answer is contested.
why_digital: Dossiers and decisions move electronically between labs and the contractor.

why_ai: The product is physical specimens handled under consent and storage rules, sourced through trusted site relationships.
why_clarity: Orders specify specimen type, annotations and volume, recurring across clients with checkable delivery.
why_digital: Physical samples are collected, stored and shipped, though buyers order remotely from anywhere.

why_ai: Deal judgement and integration planning are high-stakes and relationship-driven, though analysis is increasingly tool-assisted.
why_clarity: Each deal is different and success shows only after integration years later.
why_digital: Diligence data and models are digital, but deals are negotiated in person with local health systems.

why_ai: Rate-setting is an accountable statutory function that no vendor can take over, though the computation is mechanical.
why_clarity: Weighted medians are computed by a statutory formula on reported data, repeated each cycle.
why_digital: Reported data and published rates are entirely digital, set nationally.

why_ai: Government surveyors inspect labs in person under statutory authority, and New York's reviewers approve tests under state law.
why_clarity: Inspections follow written regulations, but findings depend on the surveyor and outcomes are slow to show.
why_digital: Inspections happen on site in each state; reports are digital.

why_ai: Advocacy and convening depend on member relationships and standing with regulators.
why_clarity: Advocacy success is hard to define and shows up only in legislation or court rulings years later.
why_digital: Work is a mix of in-person meetings and digital publishing.

why_ai: News and analysis are directly substitutable by AI summarisation, leaving trusted editors as the only defence.
why_clarity: Issues follow a recurring format, but quality is judged by subscribers' taste.
why_digital: Entirely digital publishing sold online.
